title: Ahead, Back & Nearby
intro: Children sharpen their sense of space by pointing just ahead, looking back, and pulling trusted adults closer. Today we add 3 practical location words for fine-tuning directions with auto drivers, delivery agents, and visitors.

words.babyAnalogy: Stretching one arm forward to point a little farther along the path.
words.actionTag: When your auto should continue past the current spot, point forward and say 'Swalpa munde' (A little ahead).

words.babyAnalogy: Turning the head and pointing over one shoulder at what was passed.
words.actionTag: When a visitor walks past the correct door, point back and say 'Hinde hogi' (Go back).

words.babyAnalogy: Pulling both hands inward to bring someone or something closer.
words.actionTag: When a delivery agent is standing too far away, beckon gently and say 'Hattira banni' (Come closer).

combos.context: Combining Swalpa and Nillisi (Lesson 4) + Munde (Lesson 8) for an auto ride.

quiz.scenario: Your auto is almost at your gate, but the driver starts stopping a few metres too early.
quiz.question: What phrase asks the driver to stop a little ahead?
quiz.explanation: Swalpa (A little, Lesson 4) + Munde (Ahead) + Nillisi (Stop politely, Lesson 4) = Stop a little ahead, please.

quiz.scenario: A technician walks past your apartment door and needs to retrace a few steps.
quiz.question: How do you politely direct them back?
quiz.explanation: Hinde (Back) + Hogi (Go politely, Lesson 3) = Go back, please.

quiz.scenario: A delivery agent is at the far end of the lobby, and you want them to approach you.
quiz.question: What do you say while beckoning gently?
quiz.explanation: Hattira (Near / Close) + Banni (Come politely, Lesson 3) = Come closer, please.
